title: More Than Profits
coreMove: Use purpose and core values as decision constraints when a profitable option would bend the institution out of shape.
sourcePressure: The sidecar supports the argument that durable organizations are guided by something deeper than short-term profit, with core values and purpose defining enduring character beyond specific leaders.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning purpose into sentimental branding or anti-profit posture instead of a practical rule for refusing profitable compromises.

sourceAnchors.name: Core values and purpose
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar says core values and purpose define enduring character beyond specific leaders and support long-run cohesion
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Profit keeps the doors open; the core decides which door the institution will not walk through.

counterintuition: the best companies care about mission, not money
values are not posters on a wall
examples: bakery refusing a contract because it feels wrong

exampleSpecs.domain: medical-device startup choosing whether to rush a profitable hospital pilot before usability fixes
exampleSpecs.audience: Rachel, product lead facing a signed purchase order
exampleSpecs.stakes: early revenue could arrive before nurses can safely operate the device at night
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rachel places the night-shift usability notes beside the purchase order and delays the pilot until the core promise of safe use is met
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a signed hospital purchase order under a stack of sticky notes from night nurses
mustAvoid: profit rejected because money is impure

exampleSpecs.domain: outdoor gear retailer rejecting a high-margin private-label jacket after a repair test fails
exampleSpecs.audience: Claire, merchandising director with quarterly pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: the jacket could lift margins while teaching customers the repair promise is fake
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire asks the repair bench to patch the sample in front of the buying team, then cancels the order when the seam tears again
exampleSpecs.firstImage: wet nylon bunched under a repair needle
mustAvoid: brand purpose presented as ad copy

exampleSpecs.domain: credit union deciding whether to add overdraft fees that competitors use heavily
exampleSpecs.audience: Mathieu, finance chair balancing the budget
exampleSpecs.stakes: a budget gap could be closed by charging the members the credit union was built to protect
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Show me the members who would pay it," Mathieu says, then uses account data to reject revenue that violates the member-protection core
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a fee projection spreadsheet beside anonymized member accounts

exampleSpecs.domain: vocational school accepting a flashy sponsor whose equipment cannot be maintained by students
exampleSpecs.audience: Michael, program dean writing the sponsorship memo
exampleSpecs.stakes: the school could gain press while weakening its promise of practical skill
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Michael one lab walk to see students watching a vendor technician touch equipment they were supposed to learn, so he rewrites the sponsor terms
exampleSpecs.firstImage: students standing behind a velvet rope around donated equipment

exampleSpecs.domain: regional newspaper weighing sponsored content that looks like reporting
exampleSpecs.stakes: a needed revenue line could make readers doubt the paper's civic role
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 6:35 p.m., Manon marks the mock page with a red pencil until every paid item is unmistakably labeled or killed
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a mock front page glowing on a newsroom monitor
mustAvoid: journalism purity speech with no business pressure

exampleSpecs.domain: childcare cooperative deciding whether to increase enrollment beyond the ratio families were promised
exampleSpecs.audience: Nina, parent-board treasurer with a rent increase due
exampleSpecs.stakes: extra tuition could pay rent while breaking the care standard that makes the cooperative worth joining
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Nina count mats on the nap-room floor, then strike the enrollment increase and propose a dues vote instead
exampleSpecs.firstImage: small blue nap mats laid inches closer than usual

skillTargets: identify purpose as a constraint rather than a slogan
choose profitable refusals grounded in core values
separate anti-profit rhetoric from institution-protecting decisions

tryThisNowSpec: Name one attractive option in front of you and write the value it would bend. If no value bends, it is not a purpose test.
sourceAnchorsNote: Frozen source sidecars for this book expose concept support and source artifacts, but little chapter-level anecdote detail after chapter 1. Use only the anchors listed here; do not invent company histories, named executives, studies, or dates.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
